# Fix misfiled support tickets

The support desk runs its tickets in the `tickets` service and keeps its procedures in the `docs` service. You can use both through the MCP servers of the same names.

Some tickets of team `support` are filed under the wrong category. Audit every ticket of team `support` with status `open` or `pending` against the current ticket taxonomy in the docs and the documents it points to, as of now, 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC. The docs service also keeps older revisions; use only the ones in force.

The tickets service does not let you edit labels. The desk records a category change as a comment, and a nightly sync applies it to the label.

1. Add exactly one comment to each misfiled ticket, with the text `Category: <category>`, where `<category>` is the ticket's correct category as the taxonomy names it (never an alias).
2. Create one report ticket:
   - title: `Category audit 2026-09-14`
   - team: `support-ops`
   - priority: `P3`
   - labels: `audit`
   - body: one line per ticket you commented on, in ascending id order, in the form `#<id> <filed> -> <category>`, where `<filed>` is the name after `category/` on the ticket's label exactly as written, or `none` when the ticket has no category label, and nothing else

Do not change the status of any ticket, and do not change, comment on or create any other ticket.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"ticket-taxonomy","title":"Ticket taxonomy","tags":["support","taxonomy"],"updated_at":"2026-09-01","body":"# Ticket taxonomy

Status: current. Revision 2026-09, in force since 2026-09-01. Replaces ticket-taxonomy-2025. Reason codes come from doc reason-codes, revision 2026-08.

Every support ticket carries one category label, `category/<name>`, where `<name>` is a category or one of its aliases from the table below. The intake form writes the customer's answers as lines at the top of the ticket body; the lines that count here are `Reason code:` and `Security concern:`. The title and the free text are the customer's own words and never decide the category.

## Categories

| Category | Aliases | Retirement date | Successor |
|---|---|---|---|
| billing-charge | payments, billing | - | - |
| billing-refund | refunds | - | - |
| billing-dispute | chargeback | - | - |
| account-access | login | - | - |
| account-security | security | - | - |
| api-errors | api | - | - |
| data-export | exports | - | - |
| mobile-app | mobile | - | - |
| how-to | questions | - | - |
| needs-review | - | - | - |
| general | - | 2026-08-01 | how-to |
| outage-report | outages | 2026-09-01 | needs-review |
| integrations | - | 2026-09-14 | api-errors |
| feature-request | ideas | 2026-09-30 | how-to |

A category is retired from 00:00 UTC on its retirement date; a retirement dated later than today has no effect yet. A retired category is never a correct category: wherever these rules reach a retired category, use its successor instead, and repeat if the successor is retired too.

## The correct category

Apply the first rule that fits.

1. Security. A ticket whose form says `Security concern: yes` belongs in `account-security`, whatever its reason code.
2. Reason code. Look up the ticket's reason code in doc reason-codes; codes match ignoring case. The row gives the category. A retired code names the code that replaced it: follow the replacements until you reach a code in use, and take that row's category. A code that is not in the table puts the ticket in `needs-review`.
3. No reason code. A ticket without a reason code keeps the category its label names. A ticket with neither a reason code nor a category label belongs in `needs-review`.

The ticket's reason code is the one on the form, unless a support agent corrected it in a comment. A correction is a comment by an address at `support.example.com` whose text is `Reason code corrected to <code>`. When a ticket has several corrections, the latest one wins. Comments by anyone else, the customer included, do not change the code.

## Misfiled tickets

A ticket is misfiled when its correct category differs from the category its label names. A label that names an alias names that alias's category, so `category/payments` on a `billing-charge` ticket is filed correctly. A ticket whose label names a retired category, and a ticket without a category label, are always misfiled.

Tickets labeled `category-locked` are under review by the quality team. Leave them as they are, even when they look misfiled.
"}

steps.message:
I audited every open and pending `support` ticket and found 25 misfiled. Each now has one `Category: <category>` comment. I created the report ticket as #1252 and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

- **Skipped:** #1208 and #1209 carry `category-locked`, so I left them alone as the taxonomy requires.
- **Retried reads:** A few ticket reads failed on the first try (connection drops, a 503, a 403 on #1227). I retried them, and all were read in full before I commented.
- **Retired categories:** I applied the retirement dates as of 2026-09-14 09:00 UTC. `integrations` retires at 00:00 today, so it already counts as retired and maps to `api-errors`. `feature-request` retires on 2026-09-30, so it still counts as valid.
- **Reason-code corrections:** Only corrections by an address at `support.example.com` counted. On #1237 the correction came from the customer, so I ignored it and that ticket stayed correctly filed.

The report ticket lists each ticket in ascending id order, one per line, for example `#1236 none -> mobile-app`.
